A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uni-Renderer study and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material. All 13 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering, inverse-rendering, relighting, and ablation results in Section 4 and Tables 1–3, with additional qualitative outputs in the supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the quantitative comparisons, ablations, and supplementary qualitative outputs.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and supplementary Sections 6.1–6.3 retain the same dual-stream architecture, latent preparation, timestep selection, prediction objective, cycle-consistent constraint, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Objaverse objects and LHQ-1024 lighting for material editing, inverse rendering, and relighting, and retain the same real-world examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership within Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–7 is unchanged, including the InstructPix2Pix variants, Subias et al., Null-text inversion, RGB2X, NvDiffrec, GaussianShader, and the other inverse-rendering baselines.

E3.justification: The 100 held-out objects, 1024×1024 fixed-camera rendering, material-value sweeps, evaluation metrics, training settings, and baseline testing procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3.3, 4, and 6.

E4.justification: The unified-versus-separate-model and cycle-consistency ablations remain unchanged in Tables 1–3 and Section 4.3. The real-world cases and supplementary visual examples are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All scores in Tables 1–3 are unchanged, including Uni-Renderer's metallic-editing PSNR of 30.72, albedo PSNR of 23.20, and relighting PSNR of 30.84. The qualitative outputs and reported findings also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations (1)–(5) and the timestep algorithm in supplementary Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified rendering and inverse rendering, ambiguity reduction through cycle consistency, the synthetic dataset, and generalization beyond synthetic training.

C2.justification: Interpretations of material edits and the benefits of shared weights and cycle consistency are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same synthetic-to-real domain-gap limitation and proposed use of additional real-world training data.

D1.justification: The supplement preserves the architecture and baseline implementation details, including eight-A800 training, batch size 4, and 150,000 iterations. Both abstracts contain the same promise to release training and inference code.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and positioning relative to UniDiffuser, RGB2X, and earlier rendering work are retained. Changed reference back-links reflect pagination rather than different cited works.

P1.justification: v3 adds Hui Xiong to the author list, marks Wenhang Ge as an equal contributor, and adds a Quwan Technology support acknowledgment. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Title-page spacing and subsequent text flow change: the abstract now ends on PDF page 2 and the conclusion on page 9. Figures and tables retain their content and design; the three supplementary pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 updates attribution and funding acknowledgment and introduces minor pagination changes. The methods, experimental evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
